insets.title: The gate, the edge of the light

notes: The far field lies on the lower terraces about 150 m south-west of the gate, and the path from the threshing floor drops over a terrace wall 20 m above the team, where Dan's torch first shows.

The moon stands low in the east-south-east (from 335°), so every view of Amos has the road and the moonlit valley behind him and every view of Eliab has the gate lamp, the yard fire and the lit doorway behind him.
The gate lamp's light reaches about 4 m down the road; Amos stops at its edge 4.3 m from the niche, and his father comes to stand 2 m from him, inside it.
The doorway is 35 m west of the gate on the gateway's axis, so from the edge of the light Amos sees the dancers round the yard fire and, framed in the door, the robe on the north-west stool.

The house picks up Scene 14 as staged there (Asher on the north-west stool, Amos's place set on the south-west stool, Micah and an old neighbour on the end stools, drum and pipe on the sleeping bench), with Eliab dancing before the hearth, where Dan finds him.

The mantle stitch W09 to W10 carries the camera after Eliab out of the door, through the dance ring and across the dark yard, and it stops in the gateway as he walks on into the light, where it stopped in Scene 2 while his lamp went down into the valley.
At the gate the camera keeps to the lamp side of father and son, moving between Amos's shoulder (on the father) and the father's shoulder (on the son).
The spacing stays uneven: the father walks 35 m to stand 2 m from his son, Amos comes in once on the fatted calf and pulls free back to the edge of the light, and the father holds his ground.
Asher keeps his father's Stay by coming only as far as the doorway; the flinch and the sling are cuts along the 35 m axis, each after the camera has turned down the yard past the father.
